title: Toolformer: Language Models Can Teach Themselves to Use Tools
problem: Large language models struggle with basic functionality like arithmetic, factual lookup, and temporal awareness, and existing tool-use approaches rely on large amounts of human annotation or are task-specific.
method: Toolformer, a language model finetuned in a self-supervised way to decide when and how to use external tools (calculator, Q&A, search engine, translation, calendar) by filtering API calls based on whether they reduce perplexity on future tokens.
key_results: Toolformer achieves substantially improved zero-shot performance across various downstream tasks, often outperforming much larger models like GPT-3 (175B) and OPT (66B), without sacrificing core language modeling abilities.
limitations: Inability to use tools in a chain
Lack of interactive tool use (e.g., refining search queries)
Does not account for computational cost of API calls
future_work: Considering computational cost in API call decisions
key_claims: Language models can teach themselves to use external tools in a self-supervised way.
Toolformer does not require large amounts of human annotations.
Toolformer improves zero-shot performance on downstream tasks without losing generality.
Toolformer outperforms significantly larger models on several benchmarks.
